title: Fair Value Measurements - ASC 820
learning_objectives: Apply highest and best use concept

content.definition: Price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in orderly transaction between market participants at measurement date (exit price)

level_1.description: Quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities

level_2.description: Observable inputs other than Level 1 (quoted prices for similar assets, quoted prices in inactive markets, or other observable inputs)
examples: Interest rate swap valued using observable LIBOR rates
Real estate appraised using comparable sales
level_2.techniques: May require adjustments to observable inputs

level_3.description: Unobservable inputs (entity's own assumptions about what market participants would use)
examples: Valuation of privately-held company using discounted cash flows
Complex derivatives with no market data

valuation_techniques.market_approach: Uses prices and relevant info from market transactions (comparable sales)
valuation_techniques.income_approach: Converts future amounts (cash flows, earnings) to single present value (DCF)
valuation_techniques.cost_approach: Amount required to replace service capacity of asset (replacement cost)

highest_and_best_use.principle: Fair value measured based on highest and best use by market participants
highest_and_best_use.note: May differ from entity's current use
highest_and_best_use.example: Land used as parking lot, but highest and best use is commercial development - value at development use

content.nonfinancial_assets: Measured at highest and best use. Financial assets/liabilities measured at price in most advantageous market.
disclosures: Fair value measurements by level of hierarchy
cpa_exam_tips: Level 1 = Quoted prices, identical assets, active markets (most reliable)
Level 2 = Observable inputs for similar assets
Level 3 = Unobservable inputs, entity's assumptions (least reliable)
Fair value = Exit price (what you'd receive to sell)
Use Level 1 if available, then Level 2, then Level 3 as last resort

key_points: Fair value = Exit price in orderly transaction
Highest and best use for nonfinancial assets
